What Your Skin Does While You Sleep
Skin repairs itself at night while you sleep. This article explains what happens during sleep and how a 60 second evening routine supports that process.
What Your Skin Does While You Sleep
While you sleep, your skin repairs damage from the day. What you apply to your skin before bed affects how much water your skin holds during the night.
How skin changes at night

During the day, skin is exposed to sunscreen, pollution, dry office air, light from screens and stress. At night, blood flow to the skin rises, water loss from skin is highest, and the skin surface repairs itself. Dryness that builds overnight is why skin can look more tired in the morning.
That is why applying serum in the evening matters as much as applying it in the morning. Using it twice a day matches the different work skin does during the day and at night.
The 60-second evening routine
Cleanse
the skin, removing sunscreen, sweat and dirt from the air.
Serum:
2–4 pumps of PDRN Brightening Serum on clean, dry skin, face and neck.
Moisturizer
over the serum to keep water in the skin while you sleep.
Sleep.
Aim for the same sleep times each night. Skin follows the same daily schedule as the rest of the body.
Water in the skin during the night

The serum contains sodium hyaluronate, glycerin, sodium PCA and panthenol. These ingredients draw water into the skin and help the skin hold water during the night, when water loss is highest. PDRN and the peptide in the serum support an even skin tone and a rested appearance in the morning.
Tava Labs sells PDRN Brightening Serum, a daily face serum. This evening routine takes 60 seconds. Cleanse, apply the serum, apply moisturizer, then sleep.
